title: Kumulipo (Hawaiian creation chant)
summary: The Kumulipo is a Hawaiian chant of about 2,102 lines that records both creation and the descent of chiefs. Queen Liliʻuokalani dated it to 1700, while the National Park Service says it is accepted as composed in the 18th century for the chief Kalani-nui Kaʻīʻiamāmao. A text based on a manuscript owned by King Kalākaua was printed in Honolulu in 1889.

uncertainty.note: EBSCO reports Liliʻuokalani's date of 1700; the National Park Service says only the 18th century. EBSCO notes the named poet lived 1716-1784, so the 1700 date and the poet's attribution cannot both hold.

as_recorded.value: composed in 1700 by the poet Keāulumoku

where.modern_name: Hawaiian Islands (proxy pin at the archipelago centre; the opened sources do not say where the chant was composed)
where.historical_name: The Hawaiian Islands before the unified kingdom

importance.justification: The most intact Hawaiian record of creation and chiefly genealogy.
